headline: Perturbation response models are tested for transfer and calibrated evaluation
label: Perturbation Response Model Validation
summary: Recent CRISPRi perturbation studies test whether predictive models transfer across cell lines and hold up under calibrated evaluation metrics.
synthesis: The common thread is how predictive models of perturbation response are evaluated and how far their outputs carry beyond the fitting setting. The Virtual Cell Challenge 2026 metrics are calibrated on experimental repeats for zero-shot CRISPRi transcriptional response prediction, anchoring evaluation to measured reproducibility. The CASTER study addresses transfer of CRISPRi knockdown responses across four human cell lines and reports that adaptation requires screening part of each target line, making transfer conditional rather than automatic. OCCAM and GAIN focus on model architecture: OCCAM combines denoised single-cell representations with gene interaction, text and protein features, while GAIN decomposes combinatorial responses into an additive baseline plus a learned interaction term. CIRCE uses Boltzmann distributions over Hamming distance to infer graded signaling activity. Taken together, the shared element is an explicit reliability question: calibrated metrics and transfer conditions are reported alongside predictive performance.
